title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two Rio Arriba County sisters sued Española over a July 23 traffic stop. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, and her 12-year-old sister, identified as DD, say a Flock Safety camera wrongly flagged their car as stolen from Rio Rancho. The plate differed by one digit, ending in 2 but read as 7, according to lawsuits filed Jan. 3 in state District Court. Española officers stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed them, and put them in police vehicles before finding the error. Jaclynn asked officers to call their mother for the younger girl, but the girl was handcuffed and placed in another police car, the complaints say. The sisters seek unspecified damages and compensation for personal injuries, including anxiety, fear, worry, and restricted movement.

Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, filed a similar April lawsuit for Adam Pacheco, then 17, who was mistakenly targeted as an armed robbery suspect and forced to kneel in the road. Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The article does not say what happens next beyond the pending lawsuits.
